_comment: long-doc-permutator, SAFE sizing. Sends the same context documents in different orders.  ***CORRECTION 2026-08-30: this does NOT isolate 'LMCache chunk-level reuse that survives reordering'. There is no such reuse in this deployment. LMCache keys every chunk with _hash_tokens(tokens, prefix_hash=...) (token_database.py:269) -- a chained hash over everything preceding it -- so moving a context to a different position changes its key and every key after it. Reordering produces entirely new keys, not relocatable ones. Position-independent reuse is a separate feature (CacheBlend) and is not enabled here.*** What LMCache actually does on this box is fill vLLM's EVICTION gap: it is queried only on a local prefix-cache miss, and can only hit if that prefix was computed before and later evicted from the GPU pool. Measured 2026-08-30: prefix_cache_queries 1,721,256 - hits 1,042,720 = 678,536 local misses, and external_prefix_cache_queries was exactly 678,536. With GPU KV usage at 2.4% nothing is ever evicted, so a local miss means genuinely-new content LMCache cannot have either -- hence 6.6% external hit. To make this workload measure anything, the GPU pool must be SMALLER than the working set; see the sizing note below. Also note the permutations are enumerated lexicographically and truncated (long_doc_permutator.py: itertools.permutations, first ldp_num_permutations), so with N=4/P=8 six of the eight orderings start with the SAME context -- the workload is far less adversarial than it looks, which is why the LOCAL hit rate sits at 60%. Use ldp_num_permutations = N! for full diversity.  ***SIZE THIS BY OFFLOAD BYTES, NOT BY THE GPU POOL.***  total_KV = ldp_num_permutations * (ldp_system_prompt_length + ldp_num_contexts * ldp_context_length) * 11799 bytes/token.  The 11799 is LMCache's own measured cache_size_per_token for this model at world_size=1 (it prints it every run: '-> 91002 tokens/GB'). Here: 8 * (1000 + 4*6000) * 11799 = 2.36 GB, which is 59% of the 4 GiB L1 pinned-DRAM tier (--l1-size-gb 4 in ../../common/lmcache.yaml). HARD RULE: keep total_KV under ~3 GB. Once it exceeds L1, chunks flush to the /kv-l2 NVMe tier continuously, and the resulting dirty pages + pinned CUDA-IPC transfer buffers grow the shared 128 GiB unified pool until the NVIDIA driver fails an allocation -- which HARD-RESETS this node rather than OOM-killing a process (no NMI watchdog; BENCHMARK-HANDOFF.md section 3, lmcache-benchmark-report.md section 3.2). Measured points: N=5 C=5000 P=10 -> 3.07 GB ran clean; N=5 C=20000 P=20 -> 23.83 GB CRASHED THE NODE 2026-08-30. DO NOT size against the 3,260,912-token GPU KV pool: reaching GPU eviction would need ~38 GB of offload traffic, roughly 10x the crash threshold, so on this box with this L1 the eviction regime is simply not reachable. This workload does not need it -- reordering already defeats positional prefix reuse, which is the effect being measured. ldp_num_inflight_requests is 1 on purpose: concurrent in-flight prompts multiply the simultaneously-pinned transfer buffers, the acute half of the crash mechanism. MODEL MUST BE THE HF REPO ID: this workload sizes contexts in exact tokens, so it calls AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model) (tokenizers.py:104) on the SAME string it puts in the request payload (request_sender.py:240); the served name is not a repo ID so the tokenizer load fails, and the repo ID alone would 404 unless ../deployment.yaml lists it as a second --served-model-name (it does). UPSTREAM BUG WORKAROUND -- ldqa_max_output_length: long-doc-permutator has no output-length knob and ignores this value, but it MUST be present or the run dies with "max output length cannot be specified for the 'long-doc-permutator' workload". The schema item (interactive/schema.py:286) is conditioned on workload==long-doc-qa and to_namespace() only applies a schema default when the condition holds, so otherwise it resolves to None; command.py:540 uses '!= 128' as its was-this-explicitly-set sentinel and None trips it. Setting it to exactly 128 keeps the sentinel quiet. Do NOT 'clean up' this key.
